item.text:
**5B.2 Research Note**

**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning negative. Srettha did elevate at least one clearly qualified market technocrat into the finance ministry and worked through investment-promotion channels, but his government also pressured the central bank for easier money and kept a cabinet style that mixed technical appointments with Shinawatra-network patronage.

- [Thai ex-executive Pichai named finance minister, faces growth challenge](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/thai-exexecutive-pichai-named-finance-minister-faces-growth-challenge-3401984) | Reuters via Investing.com | April 28, 2024 | Pichai Chunhavajira, described by Reuters as a former energy executive and Srettha adviser, was named finance minister and deputy PM; Reuters also notes he had been chair of the Stock Exchange of Thailand and a Bank of Thailand board member. Strong positive evidence for appointing a competent economic professional. | QIDs: 5B.2

- [Thailand’s Cabinet Reshuffle Welcomes Six New Ministers](https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/52/iid/283531) | Public Relations Department, Thailand | April 29, 2024 | The official announcement says Srettha appointed Pichai Chunhavajira, previously chair of the SET board, as finance minister and deputy PM. This is direct state-source evidence for a technocratic economic appointment. | QIDs: 5B.2

- [Mr. Narit Therdsteerasukdi, Secretary General of the Thailand Board of Investment (BOI) accompanied Mr. Srettha Thavisin, Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, on a visit to Australia](https://www.boi.go.th/en/boi_event_detail/?module=activity&topic_id=135122) | Thailand Board of Investment | March 4-6, 2024 | Srettha traveled with the BOI secretary general to promote investment policy, business facilitation, and talks with major firms. This supports a reading that he worked through a professional economic agency rather than purely political operatives. | QIDs: 5B.2, 5B.1

- [Thai central bank holds key rate, defies government calls for cuts](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/thai-central-bank-holds-key-rate-defies-government-calls-for-cuts-3372713) | Reuters via Investing.com | April 10, 2024 | Reuters reported the Bank of Thailand resisted repeated government calls to lower rates to support growth. This is negative evidence because Srettha’s camp was pressing an independent technocratic institution rather than clearly empowering it. | QIDs: 5B.2, 5B.1

- [Daughter of Thai heavyweight Thaksin calls central bank independence an ‘obstacle’](https://theprint.in/world/daughter-of-thai-heavyweight-thaksin-calls-central-bank-independence-an-obstacle/2068725/) | Reuters via ThePrint | May 3, 2024 | Reuters says Srettha had repeatedly pressed the central bank to cut rates, and Paetongtarn called BOT independence an obstacle. This points to a political camp trying to subordinate technocratic independence to growth politics. | QIDs: 5B.2

- [Forty Thai senators seek PM’s dismissal over cabinet appointment](https://theprint.in/world/forty-thai-senators-seek-pms-dismissal-over-cabinet-appointment/2089532/) | Reuters via ThePrint | May 17, 2024 | Reuters reported that senators challenged Srettha over appointing Pichit Chuenban, a politically connected former lawyer for the Shinawatra family with a contempt conviction history. While not an economic post, it is the clearest evidence that his cabinet choices still included loyalist/patronage figures rather than a clean technocratic-only pattern. | QIDs: 5B.2

**Gap:** I did not find a clean 2024 source showing Srettha explicitly delegated day-to-day economic policy to a technocratic team insulated from political pressure. The strongest positive evidence is the Pichai appointment and BOI-facing conduct; the strongest negative evidence is central-bank pressure plus a cabinet style that still tolerated patronage picks.
